\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اسباب} \fa{بازی} (asbâb bâzi)}{اسباب بازی (asbâb bâzi)}]{\fa{اسباب} \fa{بازی} (asbâb bâzi) — a toy}

\label{lesson:FA-C503-asbab-bazi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a pram, then the Persian for to breastfeed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اسباب} \fa{بازی}}
\textbf{\fa{اسباب} \fa{بازی}} (\emph{asbâb bâzi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a toy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اتاق} \fa{بچه} \fa{پر} \fa{از} \fa{اسباب} \fa{بازی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{otâq-e bachche por az asbâb bâzi ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child's room is full of toys.
\end{quote}

\emph{asbâb} 'things, gear' (an Arabic plural) + \emph{bâzi} 'play'. Plural \emph{asbâb bâzihâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{asbâb bâzi} is built in Persian on \emph{asbâb}, 'things, gear', a loan usually traced to the Arabic plural \emph{asbāb}, and native \emph{bâzi}, 'play': play things.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asbâb bâzi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asbâb bâzi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{asbâb bâzi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a pram, then the Persian for to breastfeed, then say \emph{asbâb bâzi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{اسباب} \fa{بازی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A toy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عروسک} ('arusak)}{عروسک ('arusak)}]{\fa{عروسک} ('arusak) — a doll}

\label{lesson:FA-C503-arusak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to breastfeed, then the Persian for a toy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عروسک}}
\textbf{\fa{عروسک}} (\emph{'arusak}) — \textquotedblleft{}a doll\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دخترم} \fa{با} \fa{عروسکش} \fa{حرف} \fa{میزند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dokhtaram bâ 'arusakash harf mizanad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My daughter talks to her doll.
\end{quote}

Literally 'little bride': \emph{'arus} 'bride' + the diminutive \emph{-ak}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'arusak} is built in Persian on \emph{'arus}, 'bride', which was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ʿarūs}, 'bride, groom' (EtymDB), with the native diminutive \emph{-ak}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'arusak}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'arusak}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'arusak}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to breastfeed, then the Persian for a toy, then say \emph{'arusak} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بچه} \fa{داری} (bachchedâri)}{بچه داری (bachchedâri)}]{\fa{بچه} \fa{داری} (bachchedâri) — childcare, bringing up children}

\label{lesson:FA-C503-bachchedari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a toy, then the Persian for a doll.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بچه} \fa{داری}}
\textbf{\fa{بچه} \fa{داری}} (\emph{bachchedâri}) — \textquotedblleft{}childcare, bringing up children\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{داری} \fa{کار} \fa{سختی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchedâri kâr-e sakhti ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Bringing up children is hard work.
\end{quote}

\emph{bachche} 'child' + \emph{dâr} 'keeping' (stem of \emph{dâshtan}) + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bachchedâri} is built on native Persian \emph{bachche}, 'child', which EtymDB traces to a Middle Persian word for 'child, baby, cub' (EtymDB), and \emph{dâr}, the stem of \emph{dâshtan}, 'to have, to keep'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a toy, then the Persian for a doll, then say \emph{bachchedâri} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{لوس} (lus)}{لوس (lus)}]{\fa{لوس} (lus) — spoiled (of a child)}

\label{lesson:FA-C503-lus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a doll, then the Persian for childcare.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{لوس}}
\textbf{\fa{لوس}} (\emph{lus}) — \textquotedblleft{}spoiled (of a child)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدربزرگ} \fa{نوه} \fa{اش} \fa{را} \fa{لوس} \fa{کرده} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedarbozorg naveash râ lus karde ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandfather has spoiled his grandchild.
\end{quote}

\emph{lus kardan} — to spoil; \emph{lus shodan} — to act spoilt. Colloquial.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lus} is a colloquial Persian word, but no source used here gives its history, and its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قایم} \fa{موشک} (qâyem mushak)}{قایم موشک (qâyem mushak)}]{\fa{قایم} \fa{موشک} (qâyem mushak) — hide-and-seek}

\label{lesson:FA-C503-qayem-mushak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for childcare, then the Persian for spoiled.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قایم} \fa{موشک}}
\textbf{\fa{قایم} \fa{موشک}} (\emph{qâyem mushak}) — \textquotedblleft{}hide-and-seek\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{در} \fa{حیاط} \fa{قایم} \fa{موشک} \fa{بازی} \fa{میکنند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchehâ dar hayât qâyem mushak bâzi mikonand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children are playing hide-and-seek in the yard.
\end{quote}

\emph{qâyem} 'hidden' + \emph{mushak} 'little mouse': hiding like a mouse.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qâyem mushak} is built in Persian on colloquial \emph{qâyem}, 'hidden', usually traced to Arabic \emph{qāʾim}, and native \emph{mush}, 'mouse', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{mūš}, with the diminutive \emph{-ak}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
